name: Mui Ne Beach Strip
tagline: The kitesurfing coast, one road along the sand
description: The twenty-kilometre strip of guesthouses, resorts, kite schools and beach bars running along the coast road northeast of Phan Thiet. It is where every foreign visitor stays, where the wind is, and where the international community such as it is concentrates from November to April.
bestFor: Anyone here for the wind, with the schools and the bars on the strip
pros: Kite schools, gear shops and the wind directly there
The whole international scene along one road
Beach bars and restaurants for the season
cons: Strung out over twenty kilometres, so a motorbike is essential
Much of it closes from May to October
Beach erosion has taken sections of the sand

name: Phan Thiet Town
tagline: The working city, with the fishing fleet in the river mouth
description: The actual city, five kilometres southwest of the strip, built around the Ca Ty river where hundreds of blue wooden fishing boats pack the water. It has the markets, the banks, the hospital and the ordinary Vietnamese life that the beach road does not, at a fraction of the prices.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting local prices and a real Vietnamese city
pros: Local prices for everything, roughly half the strip
The fishing harbour is genuinely remarkable
cons: No beach scene and little English
Noisy and hot with little shade

name: Ham Tien
tagline: The middle of the strip, where the Russian community settled
description: The section of the beach road where the long-standing Russian and eastern European presence concentrated, with restaurants, shops and services in Cyrillic alongside Vietnamese. It has the densest cluster of amenities on the strip and the most year-round activity of any part of it.
bestFor: Season stays wanting the most services within walking distance
pros: The densest run of restaurants and shops on the strip
Central for the main kite spots
cons: Very specific demographic that is not for everyone
Traffic on the single coast road

name: Suoi Nuoc and the Northern Bays
tagline: Past the dunes, the quieter end of the coast
description: The coast northeast beyond Mui Ne village, past the red and white sand dunes, where the development thins into a few resorts on quieter bays. The wind is often better here and the crowds are absent. It is remote enough that a motorbike and some self-sufficiency are required.
bestFor: Kitesurfers wanting emptier water and quiet
pros: Emptier beaches and often better wind
cons: Twenty-five minutes from anything on a motorbike
Almost nothing open out of season

name: Ke Ga and the Southern Coast
tagline: The lighthouse coast southwest of the city
description: The stretch of coast southwest of Phan Thiet towards Ke Ga, where a French colonial lighthouse stands on a rock island offshore and the coast is dragon fruit farms and quiet beaches. It is much less developed than Mui Ne and considerably cheaper, with almost no foreign presence.
bestFor: Stays wanting an empty coast at the lowest prices
pros: Empty beaches and the Ke Ga lighthouse
Very low prices and no tourist economy
cons: Thirty to forty minutes from Phan Thiet
No wind scene and no community
